title: Set Up GA4 and Build a Marketing Dashboard
tools_required: A website OR Google Merchandise Store Demo Account
learning_outcomes: Create and configure a GA4 property with proper event tracking
Set up Google Tag Manager to fire custom events
Build exploration reports that reveal user behavior insights
Create a funnel visualization to identify drop-off points
Connect GA4 to Looker Studio and build a professional dashboard

steps.title: Create GA4 Property and Install via GTM
steps.instructions:
1. Go to https://analytics.google.com and sign in with your Google account.
2. If you don't have a website to track, use the GA4 Demo Account: Go to https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/6367342 and click 'Access Demo Account'. This gives you real data from the Google Merchandise Store.
3. If using your own site: Click Admin (gear icon) > Create > Property. Name it 'TechPath Marketing Dashboard'. Set timezone to India (GMT+5:30) and currency to INR.
4. Go to https://tagmanager.google.com and create a new GTM container (type: Web).
5. Copy the GTM installation code (two snippets). Install the first snippet in the <head> of your website, and the second after the opening <body> tag.
6. In GTM, create a new Tag:
   - Tag type: Google Analytics: GA4 Configuration
   - Measurement ID: Your GA4 Measurement ID (find it in GA4 > Admin > Data Streams > your stream > Measurement ID, starts with G-)
   - Trigger: All Pages
7. Click Preview in GTM to test. Visit your website in the new tab that opens.
8. In GTM Preview panel, verify the GA4 Configuration tag fired on 'Container Loaded'.
9. Go to GA4 > Reports > Realtime and verify you can see your own visit.
10. Once confirmed working, click Submit in GTM to publish the container.
11. Take a screenshot of: GTM workspace showing the GA4 tag, and GA4 Realtime report showing your visit.

steps.title: Configure Key Events (page_view, scroll, click, form_submit)
steps.instructions:
1. In GA4, go to Admin > Data Streams > your stream > Enhanced Measurement. Verify these are ON:
   - Page views (always on)
   - Scrolls (fires at 90% scroll depth)
   - Outbound clicks
   - Site search
   - File downloads
   - Video engagement
2. Now create CUSTOM events in GTM. Go to your GTM container.
3. Create Event 1 — CTA Button Click:
   - New Tag > GA4 Event
   - Event Name: cta_click
   - Parameters: Add 'button_text' = {{Click Text}}, 'page_location' = {{Page URL}}
   - Trigger: Create new trigger > Click - All Elements > Some Clicks > Click Classes contains 'cta' OR Click Text contains 'Enroll' OR Click Text contains 'Buy' (adjust to your site's CTA buttons)
4. Create Event 2 — Form Submission:
   - New Tag > GA4 Event
   - Event Name: form_submit
   - Parameters: Add 'form_id' = {{Form ID}} (create a Data Layer Variable or use Click ID)
   - Trigger: Create new trigger > Form Submission > All Forms (or specific form)
5. Create Event 3 — Scroll to 50% (custom depth):
   - New Tag > GA4 Event
   - Event Name: scroll_50
   - Trigger: Create new trigger > Scroll Depth > Vertical Scroll Depths > Percentages: 50
6. Preview and test all 3 events by performing the actions on your site.
7. In GA4, go to Admin > Events and verify your custom events appear (may take a few hours).
8. Mark 'form_submit' as a Key Event (conversion): Go to Admin > Key Events > New Key Event > type 'form_submit'.
9. Take screenshots of: All 3 GTM tags, the trigger configurations, and Preview mode showing events firing.

steps.title: Build Free Form Exploration Report
steps.instructions:
1. In GA4, go to Explore (left sidebar, looks like a squiggly line icon).
2. Click 'Blank' to start a new exploration from scratch.
3. Name it 'Page Performance by Device — Last 28 Days'.
4. Set the date range to 'Last 28 days'.
5. Add Dimensions (click the + next to Dimensions):
   - Page path and screen class
   - Device category
   - Session source/medium
6. Add Metrics (click the + next to Metrics):
   - Sessions
   - Engaged sessions
   - Engagement rate
   - Average engagement time per session
   - Conversions (if available)
   - Bounce rate
7. Configure the report:
   - Technique: Free form (default)
   - Rows: Drag 'Page path and screen class' here
   - Columns: Drag 'Device category' here
   - Values: Drag 'Sessions' and 'Engagement rate' here
8. Add a Filter: Page path does not contain '/admin' or any internal pages.
9. Set Row limit to 25 to see more pages.
10. Analyze the data:
    - Which pages have highest engagement on mobile vs desktop?
    - Which pages have the lowest engagement rate (below 40%)? These need improvement.
    - Are there pages popular on one device but not another?
11. Click the pencil icon on the exploration name and rename it clearly.
12. Take a screenshot of the complete Free Form exploration with data visible.
13. Write down 3 insights you can identify from this data (you will need these for your submission).

steps.title: Build Funnel Exploration
steps.instructions:
1. Still in GA4 Explore, click the + button to create a new exploration.
2. This time, select 'Funnel exploration' from the technique templates.
3. Name it 'User Conversion Funnel'.
4. Set date range to Last 28 days.
5. Configure Funnel Steps (click the pencil icon next to Steps):
   - Step 1: 'Visit Site' — Event: session_start
   - Step 2: 'View Key Page' — Event: page_view, add condition: page_path contains '/courses' or '/products' (use a key page on your site)
   - Step 3: 'Engage with CTA' — Event: cta_click (or scroll, if cta_click has no data yet)
   - Step 4: 'Submit Form' — Event: form_submit (or purchase for demo account)
6. Important Settings:
   - Toggle 'Make open funnel' to OFF (this means users must go through steps in order)
   - If data is sparse, toggle it ON (allows users to enter at any step)
7. Add a Breakdown:
   - Drag 'Session source/medium' or 'Device category' to the Breakdown section
   - This shows how different traffic sources perform through your funnel
8. Analyze the funnel:
   - What is the overall completion rate (Step 1 to final step)?
   - Where is the biggest drop-off? (Which step loses the most users?)
   - Do mobile users drop off more than desktop users?
   - Which traffic source has the best funnel completion rate?
9. Try changing the visualization from 'Standard funnel' to 'Trended funnel' — this shows how the funnel performance changes over time.
10. Take a screenshot of both the standard funnel view and the trended funnel view.
11. Write down: The biggest drop-off point and 2 ideas for how you would fix it.

steps.title: Connect GA4 to Looker Studio and Build Dashboard
steps.instructions:
1. Go to https://lookerstudio.google.com and sign in.
2. Click 'Blank Report' or '+ Create' > 'Report'.
3. Add Data Source:
   - Click 'Add data' > Google Analytics > Select your GA4 property
   - If using demo account: Search for 'GA4 - Google Merchandise Store' in the data source list
   - Click 'Add' and then 'Add to Report'
4. Set up the Dashboard Layout:
   - Click 'Theme and Layout' > Choose a clean theme or create custom (dark blue header, white body)
   - Set canvas size to Standard (landscape)
5. Add Header Section:
   - Add a rectangle shape at the top (dark blue background)
   - Add text: 'Marketing Performance Dashboard' (white, bold, 20pt)
   - Add text: 'TechPath Academy — Your Name' (white, 12pt)
6. Add KPI Scorecards (top row, below header):
   - Insert > Scorecard for: Total Users (with comparison to previous period)
   - Insert > Scorecard for: Sessions
   - Insert > Scorecard for: Engagement Rate (format as percentage)
   - Insert > Scorecard for: Conversions (Key Events)
   - For each: Click the scorecard > Style > Show comparison (set to Previous period)
7. Add Charts:
   - Time Series chart: Daily sessions over last 30 days (metric: Sessions, dimension: Date)
   - Pie Chart: Session default channel group (shows traffic source distribution)
   - Table: Dimension = Landing page, Metrics = Sessions, Engagement rate, Conversions. Sort by Sessions descending. Limit to 10 rows.
   - Bar Chart: Dimension = Device category, Metric = Sessions + Engagement rate
8. Add Interactivity:
   - Insert > Date range control (place in top-right corner)
   - Insert > Drop-down list control for Channel grouping (optional)
9. Final Touches:
   - Align all elements neatly (use Arrange > Distribute evenly)
   - Add borders or background colors to section off KPIs from charts
   - Check mobile view: File > Preview to see how it looks
10. Share the dashboard: Click Share > Get link > Set to 'Anyone with the link can view'.
11. Take a screenshot of the final dashboard.
12. Write your analysis (200 words): What are the top 3 insights a marketing manager should act on based on this dashboard?
